issues.explanation: In this classical construction, 为 means “to be,” not “as.”
Here 之后 means descendant or offspring, not the temporal word “after.”
In 孝母, 孝 is a verb meaning to be filial to one’s mother; the noun-oriented gloss is misleading.
The gloss is unrelated to the sentence and obscures 家’s meaning here.
In 看榜, 看 means to read or look at a posted list, not “to look after.”
In 共举大事, 举 means to undertake or launch a major undertaking; a variant-only gloss is not useful.
投军 is a useful dictionary word meaning to join the army, but it is split into 投 and 军 here.
issues.suggested_fix: Group as 投军: to join the army

issues.explanation: 在 marks the location or authority under which the troops serve; “to exist” is incorrect here.
Here 万 is the number ten thousand, not a character used in the surname 万俟.
关羽 is a personal name and must remain a single name segment; splitting it hides the character’s name.
issues.suggested_fix: Keep 关羽 together as a name: Guan Yu

issues.explanation: In this military context, 退兵 is a useful compound meaning to withdraw troops; splitting it loses that local meaning.
issues.suggested_fix: Group as 退兵: to withdraw troops

issues.explanation: Here 令 means to order or command, not the unrelated dictionary-reference gloss.
In 山左右, 山 means mountain; the surname gloss is incorrect in this context.
出战 is a useful verb meaning to go into battle or engage in combat, but it is split into 出 and 战.
issues.suggested_fix: Group as 出战: to go into battle

issues.explanation: Here 百 means one hundred, not the surname Bai.
风火 is an unnatural grouping here. The sentence has 大风 (“strong wind”) followed by 火攻 (“fire attack”).
issues.suggested_fix: Split as 风 and 火攻

issues.explanation: 攻 is part of the useful compound 火攻, meaning an attack using fire.
issues.suggested_fix: Group with 火 as 火攻: to attack with fire
